author: reek
body: A single-line text field on the GOP framebuffer (B2.1). Scancodes come from the kernel key-buffer cell -- fed by the keyboard IRQ the runtime-init spine installs (GopKey), and by the USB HID pump when the machine's keyboard is USB (H2b): the read loop takes a UsbKbd and polls through kbd-take, which pumps the interrupt endpoint and then consumes the cell. With no USB keyboard the pump is a flag test and the loop is unchanged. The kernel keyboard chapter's pure layout machinery (kb-process-scancode) turns scancodes into CCE characters with shift, caps, and dead-key handling. The field echoes as it edits, draws a block cursor after the text, supports backspace, and can mask its echo with asterisks for passphrase entry. Enter returns the buffer.

author: reek
body: The field paints its own background one cursor cell wider than its capacity, draws the text (or one asterisk per character when masked), and places a solid block cursor in the cell after the last character.

author: val
body: Extended keys arrive as an 0xE0 prefix (ignored as a break code by the layout) followed by a plain make code that collides with the numpad: an arrow key would otherwise type a digit. A single-line field has no cursor movement, so every navigation make code is simply ignored.

author: val
body: Each key event also samples the HPET main counter (0xFED00000 + 0xF0, megahertz-rate) and the timer tick cell, folding them into an entropy accumulator the caller receives beside the text -- keystroke timing the machine cannot predict. On hardware without an HPET at the standard base the read degrades to a constant and the accumulator still carries the tick cell and scancode sequence.
